name: Screens & Development
blurb: Effects on language, attention, sleep, feeding and weight

claims.claim: Higher screen time is associated with shorter sleep in young children
claims.testedAs: Higher screen time is associated with shorter sleep in young children

nhs.says: A lot of screen time is linked to poorer sleep, among other effects on health and development.

aap.says: Children with a lot of media exposure fall asleep later and sleep less; even babies can be overstimulated and lose sleep.

claims.query: screen time young children sleep duration association

claims.claim: Higher screen time is associated with higher BMI in early childhood
claims.testedAs: Higher screen time is associated with higher BMI in early childhood

nhs.says: A lot of screen time is linked to effects on healthy weight, among other health and development outcomes.

aap.says: Watching a lot of TV is associated with overweight and obesity in children.

claims.query: screen time early childhood body mass index obesity association

claims.claim: Higher screen time in infancy is associated with language delay
claims.testedAs: Higher screen time in infancy is associated with language delay

nhs.says: A lot of screen time is linked to poorer development, including language.

aap.says: Screen viewing before 18 months has lasting negative effects on language, reading and short-term memory.

claims.query: screen time infant toddler language delay expressive vocabulary

claims.claim: Early screen exposure is associated with later attention problems
claims.testedAs: Early screen exposure is associated with later attention problems

nhs.says: Fast-paced, over-stimulating video may affect how young children learn to concentrate, so avoid it. NHS frames this by content type, not total exposure.

aap.says: Toddlers who watch more TV are more likely to have trouble paying attention by age 7.

claims.query: early television screen exposure infant later attention problems ADHD

claims.claim: Infants learn less from video than from equivalent live interaction
claims.testedAs: Infants learn less from video than from equivalent live interaction

nhs.says: Young children learn best from back-and-forth interaction with people, not from a screen.

aap.says: For the same amount of time, a toddler learns far more from real play with you than from watching a screen.

claims.query: video deficit effect infant learning transfer live demonstration

claims.claim: Screen use during meals is associated with poorer eating behaviour
claims.testedAs: Screen use during meals is associated with poorer eating behaviour

nhs.says: Keep mealtimes screen-free. NHS gives the reason as protecting family time and interaction, not eating behaviour specifically.

aap.says: Eating in front of a screen distracts children so they keep eating past fullness, which can lead to weight gain.

claims.query: screen use during mealtime infant toddler eating behaviour intake

claims.claim: Educational apps improve learning outcomes in toddlers
claims.testedAs: Educational apps improve learning outcomes in toddlers

aap.says: App skills do not transfer to real-world learning for toddlers, though after age 2 some children do learn from well-designed educational programmes.

claims.query: educational app touchscreen toddler learning outcomes evaluation
